Compile Zig code from the R prompt

Source: R/source.R
zig_function.Rd

zig_function() compiles Zig source code into a small package in the session's temporary directory and defines its exported functions in env, the counterpart of Rcpp::cppFunction(). zig_source() does the same for a file, and zig_eval() evaluates one Zig expression.

Usage

zig_function(code, env = parent.frame(), quiet = TRUE)

zig_source(file, env = parent.frame(), quiet = TRUE)

zig_eval(expr, type = "f64")

Arguments

code

Zig source code, a character vector whose elements are lines.

env

The environment in which the functions are defined.

quiet

If FALSE, print the build result.

file

A Zig source file.

expr

A Zig expression, as a string.

type

The Zig type of the value of expr, a return type the boundary supports (for example "f64", "i32", "bool", "[]const u8").

Value

zig_function() and zig_source(): the function, if the code exports exactly one, otherwise a named list of the functions, invisibly. zig_eval(): the value of the expression.

Details

The code is placed in a generated main.zig after the lines const std = @import("std");, const builtin = @import("builtin");, const rzig = @import("rzig"); and the panic handler declaration (each left out when the code declares it), and before the registration block. Public functions marked /// @export are exported; when the code marks none, every top-level pub fn is exported. The types, errors and checks of the boundary are those of a package (scan_exports(), rzig_status()).

Builds are cached for the session by the code, the rzig version and the Zig compiler: calling zig_function() again with the same code defines the functions without compiling. A failed build is reported with the lines of code and stops with an error.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (isTRUE(find_zig(required = FALSE)$supported)) {
  twice <- zig_function("pub fn twice(x: f64) f64 { return 2 * x; }")
  twice(21)
  zig_eval("@sqrt(2.0)", type = "f64")
}
#> [1] 1.414214
# }
